body_text:
Any two Peano systems are uniquely isomorphic by a map preserving
zero and successor. More precisely, if $(N,0,S)$ and $(N',0',S')$
satisfy the Peano axioms, there is a unique bijection $f:N\to N'$
such that $f(0)=0'$ and $f(S(n))=S'(f(n))$. Thus the natural
numbers are determined up to unique structure-preserving
isomorphism.
